text: A farmer planted his rice in spring, row after row.
They were the finest little sprouts he had ever seen.
Every morning he knelt down to measure them.
"Too slow, too slow!" he grumbled, day and night.
So one night he waded out into the moonlit field,
and tugged every sprout a little higher, blade by blade.
"I helped our rice grow taller," he told his son.
The boy ran out to see what he had done.
Every single sprout lay withered, pale and dry,
its roots torn loose beneath the morning sky.
Give it water, give it light, and take it slow.
You cannot hurry what must grow.
